newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures claws back to end mixed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures claws back to end mixed.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures clawed back from early lows to end narrowly mixed, helped by pre-weekend shortcovering and a rebound in New York.
Benchmark January broke through a key chart support of $1,415 a tonne to touch a low of $1,410 on Far East selling but bounced back later in the day to end $6 lower at $1,424.
Traders noted scale-down industry price-fixing as the market made its way lower.
Activity was termed as thin and quiet with players unwilling to commit in the absence of market-moving factors.
Technically, January had earlier been well supported above $1,415, the last lows seen on November 7.
But it finally gave way this morning on the weight of growing robusta supplies and on heavy New York losses the day before.
"The market is finally moving out of the last range of $1,415-$1,450 into the $1,400-$1,430 band," said one.
In spread, Nov/Jan switch saw deals at $140 but volume was small.
In gradings, traders sdaid 121 originals were posted on Friday, bringing the total todate in November to 1,108 of which 360 were untenderable.
"This is quite sizeable and we expect more coffee to be graded next week in view of the large November premium to January," he said.
The November contract goes off the board next Friday.
New York's March arabica coffee futures fell sharply on Thursday on perceptions of growing nearby supplies from Central and South America. But it made a slight recovery on Friday.

Robusta prices are weighed upon by a seasonal supply uptrend from Vietnam and other major origins. But news a wet spell hampering robusta harvest in Vietnam's main growing area of Dak Lak was seen as mildly constructive, traders said. In other news, leaders of Brazil's coffee community will meet in the state of Bahia next week to discuss the way forward for Brazil's coffee policy. The forum will take place from November 27 to December 1 near Ilheeus in Bahia.
